sections.content: How many people are "visual merchandisers and related occupations"?

4,105 people

were counted on the census as "visual merchandisers and related occupations" in England and Wales in March 2021.

This makes this type of work the sixth least common occupation reported on the census.

Visual merchandisers develop, deliver and communicate visual concepts and strategies to promote brands, products and services in-store, in catalogues or online, and create displays of merchandise.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "visual merchandisers and related occupations", 21.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "visual merchandisers and related occupations" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "visual merchandisers and related occupations" included:

  • business and related research professionals
  • human resources and industrial relations officers
  • finance and investment analysts and advisers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "visual merchandisers and related occupations" there were more women than men (78.5% compared with 21.5%).

This means "visual merchandisers and related occupations" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "sales occupations".

Men made up 21.4% and women made up 78.6% of "visual merchandisers and related occupations"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "visual merchandisers and related occupations" included:

  • youth and community workers
  • sales administrators
  • nursing auxiliaries and assistants

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "visual merchandisers and related occupations" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "visual merchandisers and related occupations" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "visual merchandisers and related occupations", 8.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (55.5% compared with 44.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (72.1%) than self-employed (27.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Hackney, this is in the same region of London.
